summary: placeTrack only decodes the body when r.ContentLength > 0; a chunked request (ContentLength == -1) or an empty body silently skips the decode, so a caller-supplied `pos` is dropped and defaults to 0. The adminapi-7 concern that this bypasses pos validation is NOT true — validation still runs on the zero value and 0 is valid — but the supplied pos is silently ignored, misordering the placement.
scenario: Admin client (or proxy) sends PUT .../cells/{row}/{col}/tracks/{trackId} with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and body {"pos":3}. ContentLength is -1, so the `> 0` guard is false, decode is skipped, body.Pos stays 0, and the track is placed at pos 0 instead of 3. Self-inflicted (authenticated admin) and pos 0 is valid, so no security bypass — a correctness/ordering bug only.
suggested_fix: Decode unconditionally (an empty body is fine — json.Decode of an empty reader returns io.EOF which can be treated as 'no override'), or gate on `r.ContentLength != 0` and tolerate io.EOF, so chunked bodies with a real pos are honored.

summary: AdminAuth compares the bearer token to the secret with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare, which is constant-time only for equal-length inputs and returns 0 immediately when lengths differ. This leaks the admin secret's length through response timing. The content comparison itself is sound; only the length is observable.
scenario: An attacker sends bearer tokens of varying lengths and measures response latency; equal-length guesses take measurably longer (they run the full byte compare) than mismatched-length ones (short-circuit return 0). This narrows the secret length before a brute/dictionary attack. Low impact given a high-entropy secret, but it violates the project's stated constant-time requirement.
suggested_fix: Compare fixed-size digests instead of the raw bytes, e.g. sha256.Sum256(token) vs a precomputed sha256.Sum256(secret) fed to subtle.ConstantTimeCompare — the inputs are always 32 bytes, so neither length nor content leaks.

summary: searchSpotify (line 34) and importPlaylist (line 84) return the raw upstream error via err.Error() to the client at 502. Those errors wrap Spotify's HTTP status and response body verbatim (see internal/spotify/search.go: 'spotify: search: status %d: %s'). The adminapi-6 remediation routed 500s through serverError but left these 502 paths leaking upstream detail. Client is an authenticated admin and no secret is exposed, so impact is limited, but it is inconsistent with the sweep-1 leak-suppression intent.
scenario: A Spotify 429/4xx response bubbles its body (rate-limit JSON, internal endpoint paths) straight to the admin client. Not a secret leak, but surfaces upstream internals the sweep-1 pass was trying to hide.
suggested_fix: Log the wrapped error server-side and return a generic 'Spotify request failed' message, matching the aiBuild treatment (aibuild.go:54).
